quotes.text: # Accept a Canadian pre-authorized debit payment
Build a custom payment form or use Stripe Checkout to accept payments with pre-authorized debit in Canada.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Prices for all line items must be in the same currency.
The bank account has been instantly verified or verification wasn’t necessary.

findings: New raw lines 5-14 are a navigation index for this same canonical URL, pointing to Checkout and Direct API variants. Its omission of the 2025 detailed instructions is not evidence that PAD support, schemas, examples, webhook states, or test behavior were removed or deprecated. Do not add this 14-line navigation capture as a factual raw_files replacement; retain the prior full capture and scope any current verification to separately captured variants.

The existing source line 21 says all Checkout line items use cad, but the older full guide lines 22-24 and 32-36 explicitly allow cad or usd while requiring every line item in a given Checkout Session to use the same currency. Correct the source sentence. Source line 29's cad PaymentIntent is a sample currency, not a universal Direct API requirement; old line 468 says usually cad. The concept line 12 already preserves the CAD-preferred, USD-risk qualification.

Source line 32 describes processing as instant verified; old full guide line 669 says the bank account was instantly verified or verification was not necessary. The source line 45's processing webhook means submitted/processing, not final payment or guaranteed bank receipt. Fulfillment belongs after payment_intent.succeeded per old lines 754-768. Concept line 85 also compresses processing to verified and should preserve the alternative.

Preserve mandatory mandate options from old lines 61-67 and 472-478: payment_schedule and transaction_type required, interval_description conditional for interval or combined. Dashboard-managed dynamic payment methods can omit explicit payment_method_types but still need payment_method_options (old lines 54-59). Checkout subscription mode is described as unsupported in this dated capture, not a current global conclusion (old lines 26-35).

Preserve old verification and debit timing separation: instant or microdeposit verification, two microdeposits appearing in 1-2 business days, three failed attempts or 10-day timeout reverting to requires_payment_method, and up to five business days for success/failure notification after initiating debit (old lines 661-768). Target_date is 3-15 days, best effort, with weekend/holiday adjustments and incompatibility with microdeposits (old lines 373-386 and 923-936).

Retain sandbox test tokens/accounts as tests, not live settlement promises, and keep Accounts v2 preview versus Customer v1 example distinction from old lines 416-528. The new index provides routes but no fresh authority to revise those historical details.
substantive_changes: No substantive payment or integration behavior can be determined from the new 14-line index; old full content is absent because the captured root URL now selects Checkout and Direct API variants.
Current source requires material correction independently of this navigation-only delta: cad-or-usd same-session Checkout condition and processing status qualification.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Older full capture documents separate Checkout and Direct API variants at old lines 8-10 and 395-401; new raw lines 11-14 point to corresponding variant URLs.
Checkout supports cad or usd presentment for this dated guide, but all line items in one Session must share currency; CAD is safer if the customer's account cannot accept USD debit (old lines 20-44).
PAD is delayed notification; typically five business days to arrive, and PaymentIntent success/failure notice can take up to five business days (old lines 16 and 754-768).

PAD mandate authorization and conditional schedule fields, instant or microdeposit verification, 10-day verification timeout, and webhook-confirmed fulfillment remain old-capture facts (old lines 61-67, 661-768).
Old source's test tokens, account numbers and microdeposit values are sandbox examples only (old lines 148-195 and 770-810).
conflicts: Source line 21 says all Checkout line items must be cad, contradicted by old raw lines 22-24 and 32-36 allowing cad or usd with same-currency requirement.
Source line 32 and concept line 85 imply processing means verified, omitting old raw line 669's verification-was-not-necessary alternative; processing is not succeeded.
New raw index lines 11-14 contains no detailed capability or state text; promoting it as a substantive replacement would sever the source's factual provenance.
unresolved_questions: The new captured root index does not state the current contents of either variant. This comparison cannot assert present support for Checkout subscription mode, account eligibility, SDK behavior, or any changed detailed workflow without separately reviewed variant captures.
Older capture's Accounts v2 public-preview language and date-specific integration examples may have evolved; the new navigation index does not resolve their current applicability.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 9-14 are an index to Checkout and Direct API variants, whereas old raw lines 8-10 and 395-401 contained both full guides. [[source-stripe-acss-accept-payment]] should preserve the dated older factual capture and record the new routing as navigation only. The missing detailed text cannot establish that mandates, verification, payment modes, or the older integration paths were removed.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit/accept-a-payment, old raw lines 22-24 and 32-36 allowed CAD or USD line items within a single-currency Checkout Session, so [[source-stripe-acss-accept-payment]] line 21 needs correction despite the new index at lines 11-14 carrying no behavior. Old line 669 also says processing can mean instant verification or verification not required; old lines 754-768 reserve successful-payment fulfillment for succeeded, which the source and linked concept should distinguish.
